The best way to improve at something is to compete against someone slightly better than you. If I wanted to become a better fighter, I wouldn't challenge a top professional; they'd defeat me quickly and I'd learn nothing. It would be much smarter of me to spar with other amateurs and work my way up.

The same idea applies in baseball. If a major league team were to give a highly-touted rookie an excessive number of at-bats in their first season, they might struggle significantly, and the negative impact on their confidence would outweigh any lessons learned at that level. What they will likely do instead is place them in minor leagues where they consistently face players with a few years of experience, advancing them through the ranks based on their performance, not just their inherent talent.
